import os

import yaml
import pytest

from doorstop.core import builder, publisher, Tree, Item, Document
from doorstop.core.tree import Tree
from doorstop.core.item import Item
from doorstop.core.document import Document
from doorstop.core.publisher import publish
from doorstop.core.builder import build


# Helper to create a simple requirement file
def _create_req_file(path, uid="REQ001", text="This is a requirement"):
    content = {uid: text}
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        yaml.safe_dump(content, f)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Test cases derived from the abstract test cases
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

def test_U02_4__Decision_Tab__TC_001(tmp_path):
    """
    Store requirements in a permanent and secure manner
    """
    # Arrange: create a simple requirement file
    req_file = tmp_path / "REQ001.yml"
    _create_req_file(req_file)

    # Act: build the tree
    tree = build(cwd=str(tmp_path))

    # Assert: the requirement is present in the tree
    assert isinstance(tree, Tree)
    assert "REQ001" in tree
    item = tree["REQ001"]
    assert isinstance(item, Item)
    assert item.text == "This is a requirement"

def test_U02_4__Decision_Tab__TC_004(tmp_path):
    """
    Support thousands of requirements (boundary)
    """
    # Arrange: create 1000 requirement files
    for i in range(1, 1001):
        uid = f"REQ{i:04d}"
        req_file = tmp_path / f"{uid}.yml"
        _create_req_file(req_file, uid=uid, text=f"Requirement {i}")

    # Act: build the tree
    tree = build(cwd=str(tmp_path))

    # Assert: all 1000 requirements are present
    assert isinstance(tree, Tree)
    assert len(tree) == 1000
    for i in range(1, 1001):
        uid = f"REQ{i:04d}"
        assert uid in tree
        assert tree[uid].text == f"Requirement {i}"
